newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Business group wants WTO to extend trade reforms.
newsitem.headline: Business group wants WTO to extend trade reforms.

text.p: The International Chamber of Commerce (ICC), with member companies from over 130 countries, said on Sunday it is pressing ministers at the World Trade Orgnaisation meeting to start work on new areas of trade reform.
Maria Cattaui, secretary general of the ICC, said top of the list was the need to tackle customs modernisation.
"This is the nuts and bolts of world trade," Cattaui told Reuters in an interview.
She also said: "We think the WTO should begin building a consensus for a global framework of rules governing cross border investment."
Cattaui said that as traditional trade reforms such as tarriff reduction are achieved, other issues come to the surface.
"There are many coming down the turnpike at us as we lower traditional trade barriers," she said.
The ICC would also be pressing WTO governments to speed up implementation of the Uruguay round agreements and complete its unfinished business.
Ministers from the 128 member world trade body begin their inaugural five-day meeting in Singapore on Monday.
